data.cultural_impact: The name Bahula holds significant cultural importance in Hindu traditions, especially in the regions of Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand. It is believed that a child named Bahula will be blessed with abundant health, wealth, and prosperity, as reflected in the word 'Bahu' meaning 'Blessed with Cow'. Cows represent abundance, prosperity, and are considered sacred in Hinduism, thus the name Bahula is thought to be closely linked to this symbolism of bountifulness and wealth.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Bahula is considered a powerful name imbued with the blessings of the goddess Shashti. The name is believed to bring the energies of Shashti into the life of the child, bestowing upon them materials abundance and spiritual wellbeing. Shashti or Shasti is one of the aspect of the Goddess Durga and is believed to grant six forms of prosperity: wealth, happiness, courage, knowledge, sleep, and joined hands (Sign of blessings). Naming a child Bahula is thought to draw the blessings of this Goddess and bring fulfillment to all areas of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhagavata Purana mentions 'Bahula' - a virtuous monkey queen who embodied maternal love and devotion. She sacrificed her own life to save her son, Hanuman. Bahula's name signifies deep, selfless love and unwavering devotion to one's offspring.

vedic_reference.note: In Hindu mythology, Bahula is an avatar of the god Hanuman. She is known to have helped Lord Rama during his exile in the forest. The name Bahula is mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Ramayana and the Mahabharata.
